# Brand review — v1 rejected

**To:** development
**Re:** PotatoFarm.ai visual system
**Decision:** rebuild the surface. Structure, copy and code stay.

---

## The note we were given

"No gold. Gold is always generated by AI."

The absolute isn't true — plenty of good brands use gold. But the instinct
behind it is correct, and it points at a bigger problem than the one it
names. Brass on near-black **is** the house style of every generated
template on the internet right now, and in this market it is also the
Dubai-luxury cliché. Two strikes on one colour.

So we agree. But changing the accent alone would have fixed a symptom.

## What was actually wrong

The gold was one of eight tells. Swapping it for teal or purple and
shipping would have produced the same site in a different colour.

1. **Radial glow orbs behind every section.** The single clearest marker
   of generated design. Ours were three PNG-shaped gradients drifting on a
   40-second loop.
2. **Glassmorphism.** Translucent cards with backdrop blur. 2021's trend,
   2026's default.
3. **A pointer-tracked light following the cursor across cards.** We
   called it "expensive" in Phase 7. On reflection it reads as portfolio,
   not as a tool a brokerage runs its lead flow through.
4. **Everything a pill.** Buttons, badges, 20px cards. Rounded-everything
   is the most reliable generated-design signature there is.
5. **Placeholder geometric glyphs** as icons — ◧ ◉ ◈ ◇ ◆ ◐. They looked
   like something that hadn't been finished, because they were.
6. **Uniform card texture.** Three grids of near-identical rounded tiles
   with a hover lift, so the page read as one long surface instead of a
   sequence of arguments. We flagged this as a fault in the competitor's
   site in Phase 1 and then did it ourselves.
7. **Dark by default**, with no argument for it beyond "premium SaaS is
   dark".
8. **Geometric grotesk display type.** Correct, competent, and used by
   every startup since 2019.

## The direction

**Document, not dashboard.**

This business runs on title deeds, tenancy contracts, floor plans and
WhatsApp transcripts. Paper and ink is the honest material, it is
recognisably human, and no generator reaches for it.

| | |
|---|---|
| Ground | `#F4F1EA` — warm paper. Never pure white; that's a screen colour. |
| Ink | `#16181C` — 15.76:1 |
| Secondary | `#4A4E57` — 7.39:1 |
| Tertiary | `#6A6E78` — 4.52:1 |
| Seal | `#A83226` — 5.91:1 on paper, 5.91:1 reversed |

**One accent, and it has a job.** Seal red marks the next action and the
thing that is done. It appears nowhere else. A single disciplined accent
reads as decision; three accents read as decoration.

**Type.** Instrument Serif for display, Switzer for body, JetBrains Mono
for anything a document would set in a fixed width — timestamps, figures,
labels, statuses. All three free for commercial use and self-hostable.

**Structure.** Cards became cells in a ruled grid. Elevation is a hairline,
not a blur. Radius is 3px. Shadows, gradients, glass and glow are gone from
the token set entirely, so they cannot creep back in.

**The hero thread** is now set as a transcript — ruled rows, labelled
speakers, monospaced timestamps — rather than chat bubbles floating on a
gradient. It reads as evidence, which is what it is.

**The logo rail stopped moving.** Four names scrolling on a loop is a
template reflex. Set still, in a ruled row, they look like customers rather
than filler.

## What we kept

Everything below the surface. Information architecture, copy, component
structure, form logic, backend, CMS schemas, SEO, tests. The problem was
finish, not thinking.

## Verified

All ten colour pairs clear WCAG AA. Fourteen pages, zero failures on the
audit. Same standard as before, different palette.
